items.title: No local validation of the flag
items.whyItMatters: The vendor cites only its own development sites; external validation of a similar tool found moderate accuracy (claim c1).
items.opportunity: Estimate sensitivity, specificity and calibration from the local score log.

items.title: Reference standard error
items.whyItMatters: Late and missing departure timestamps misclassify patients near four hours (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Write a reference standard rule using the ward arrival time as a check and a rule for missing times.

items.title: Performance at night and by service
items.whyItMatters: Sensitivity is lower at night and for surgical admissions elsewhere (claims c1, c4); patients admitted overnight may be systematically missed.
items.opportunity: Report accuracy by time of day, weekday and admitting service.

items.title: Occupancy may explain the flag
items.whyItMatters: If the score mostly tracks occupancy, it flags busy days rather than patients who can be helped.
items.opportunity: Compare the score's discrimination with an occupancy-only reference model.

items.title: Escalation changes the outcome
items.whyItMatters: Flagged patients are escalated, which may shorten their boarding and make the flag look less accurate.
items.opportunity: Record escalation and analyse accuracy with and without escalated patients as a sensitivity analysis.

errorsFound: The need's 'more than four hours' and the reference standard's 'four hours or more' must be fixed to one definition before analysis.
reevaluation: The gaps support a local accuracy study with a documented reference standard, spectrum reporting and an occupancy comparison.
summary: Five gaps; the missing local validation and reference standard error are high severity.
